issues: The scene correctly limits itself to Mosiah 17:4 and does not merge Alma’s concealment with later events. The hiding place, identity of “them,” writing materials, and duration beyond “many days” remain unspecified; keep these visually ambiguous.

“The man King Noah was about to release” is unnamed in these verses; the supplied text establishes that both verses refer to the same person, but the scene does not state that the priests accuse him of reviling the king until verse 12.
Verse 12 describes the priests lifting their voices and the king becoming angry; “speaking emphatically” and “reacting angrily” are reasonable visual interpretations, not explicit staging details.

The verses do not name the man or identify the people who take and bind him; depicting the continuity with the preceding scene as the same man is reasonable, but his identity is not stated in this scene’s verses.
“As flames begin to scorch him” is faithful to verse 14; show the flames and scourging without adding wounds, blood, or gore. The words of his cry are not given here.

The previous scene's wording that flames begin to scorch him is supported, but the supplied text does not explicitly say he is already bound and scourged «unto death» before this moment; chronology in its summary compresses the events of verses 13–14.
The current scene's speaker is explicitly Abinadi from verse 20, but that identifying verse is outside this scene's refs; the dialogue itself is accurately quoted from verses 15–17.
The addressees are addressed as «ye» and «thy seed»; their identities and the physical setting remain unspecified. The warning and flock comparison are not present-tense events.
The scene is titled “Abinadi’s Final Words,” but verses 18–19 alone do not establish these as his final words; verse 20 says he fell after saying them.
Abinadi is shown speaking as flames scorch him, but the cited refs are verses 18–19; this action is established immediately before, in verse 14, and must not imply a different chronology.

The summary, listed explicit facts, and narration accurately reflect Mosiah 17:20. The previous scene's dialogue and summary also match verses 18–19; its inference that Abinadi speaks as flames scorch him is consistent with the text that he suffers death by fire, though flames are not described visually.

The unspecified-details note says witnesses are unspecified, but the prohibition against implying an on-screen witness treats their absence as established. The verse does not state whether witnesses were present. Also, the verse gives no location, but the empty locations array is conservative.
